items.rationale: Excel evaluates the innermost function first and works outwards: TRIM(A2), then UPPER on that result, then XLOOKUP on the cleaned code. Being written first does not mean being evaluated first.
TRIM and UPPER turn the text into SL-075, which is in row 6 of the price list with a price of 499.
XLOOKUP needs an exact match and the trailing space makes the text different from SD-120. With no match and no fourth argument the result is #N/A, which is why TRIM is needed.
Excel's XLOOKUP matches text without regard to case, so lower-case codes are found anyway. It does not ignore spaces, and UPPER does not remove them. UPPER is still useful to produce a standard code.
